utterance: Hi Samuel, I'm the doctor. I understand you've had tummy pain since last night. Can you tell me more about it — where exactly is the pain?
reply: Down here on the right side, low down. Started last night, about ten o'clock, so maybe fourteen hours. It's there all the time now. At first it sort of came and went. Maybe a seven out of ten.

awards.label: Whether the pain is constant or comes and goes

utterance: I see. Did the pain start somewhere else first — like around your belly button — before moving down to the right side?
reply: Yeah, it actually started around my belly button. It moved down to the right sometime overnight.

awards.label: Red flag: Where the pain started and whether it has moved

utterance: Have you felt sick or actually vomited? And have you had any fever, chills or sweats?
reply: Felt sick since the early hours, and I threw up once this morning. I felt hot and a bit shivery last night.

awards.label: Red flag: Fever, sweats or chills

utterance: How's your appetite been, and have your bowels been normal — any diarrhoea or constipation?
reply: I couldn't face breakfast, not hungry at all, which isn't like me. I didn't have diarrhoea, I went normally yesterday morning, nothing since.

utterance: Does it hurt more when you move, cough, or when the car went over a bump on the way here?
reply: Yeah, walking hurts. Every bump in the car on the way here was awful, and coughing is the worst.

awards.label: Red flag: Whether moving, walking or coughing makes it worse

utterance: Samuel, I've examined you and I'm concerned this is more than a stomach bug. The story — pain starting around your belly button and moving to the lower right side, with fever, feeling sick and being off your food — together with the tenderness I found in your lower right tummy, points strongly to appendicitis, which is inflammation of the appendix. This needs to be assessed in hospital today, because if it's left it can burst and cause a serious infection.
reply: Oh right. Do I really have to go straight there? I've got work tomorrow.

utterance: Yes, I'm afraid you do need to go now, today. This won't settle on its own and delaying could make things much worse. Please go straight to the emergency department — don't wait. It's important you don't eat or drink anything from now on, in case you need an operation. If the pain suddenly gets much worse, or you feel faint, dizzy or very unwell on the way, call 000 for an ambulance.
